newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Matthew Clark boosts cider adverts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Matthew Clark boosts cider adverts.

text.p: British cider maker Matthew Clark, whose share of the cider market has fallen in the face of booming "alcopop" sales and an industry price war, said that its initial goal this year is to stabilise the cider market.

To this end it has sharply increased advertising for the new financial year to 9.0 million stg from 2.0 million for its key Diamond White and Blackthorn brand ciders, as well as the launch of Blackthorn Gold.
"That is a major increase in advertising support," business development director Peter Huntley told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We believe the situation has stabilised a lot, in the cider industry and in Matthew Clark," he added.
Matthew Clark's share price plunged by about 60 percent from around 670 pence after it issued a profits warning in September. The price was up 4.0 pence at 246-1/2 pence at 0900 GMT.

The company's advertising campaign aims to reclaim drinkers who have switched over to "alcopops" -- alcoholic lemonades and sodas. Also the price war has subsided and "sanity returned this year," said Huntley.
"We're looking to stabilise the cider market in the short term and in the medium term to go back to the sort of growth we enjoyed over the past 10 years".

The cider industry grew by around seven percent annually in the 1990s but declined by around three percent in last financial year. At the same time Matthew Clark's share of the cider market slumped to 37 percent from 41 percent, while bigger rival H.P. Bulmer Holdings Plc saw its share grow to 54.5 percent -- its highest level for over 30 years.
Matthew Clark reported a four percent drop in pre-tax profit for the year to April 30 to 40.6 million stg, but maintained its total dividend of 24 pence a share.

As for current trading, Huntley said: "All the markets in which we compete -- cider, wines and wholesaling -- are all very competitive and our trading at the moment is flat. We're trading in line with our expectations".
"Our premium cider brands, particularly Diamond White, were very vulnerable to alcopops as it turned out," said Huntley.
Sales of Diamond White, the Diamond range and K cider fell by 26 percent in the year to April, in a market whose overall British sales were down by three percent.

Huntley said it was not only increased competition from "alcopops" but the disruption of integrating its Taunton Cider business -- purchased in September last year for 275 million stg -- and the price war which were to blame for losing market share to Bulmers.
The advertising campaign for Blackthorn will start in August while that for Diamond White began earlier this month. Also, the company launched Blackthorn Gold in May.
"It's still early days so we can't really comment on what we've seen coming back yet....but the way it's been received by the trade, it's going very well at the moment," said Huntley.

"We believe that the cider industry can't afford to go back into another price war which would undermine our advertising strategy, the cider industry is facing a lot of competition from all the other areas of the drinks industry," he added.
Huntley said the company had not set itself any definite market share target but once the cider market had stabilised it would like to increase its sales and market share.
"Our non-cider brands and wholesaling business are in good shape and performing to plan," chief executive Peter Aikins said in the results statement.
Its wholesale operating profits climbed to 7.0 million stg from 2.7 million in the year to April.
